sources.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro flees Brazil after presidential election loss, reports say
sources.text: The far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly fled Brazil and is on his way to the United States after losing Sunday’s presidential election to the leftwing incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who called the act “shameful”.A report by the news website Metrópoles, citing people close to the politician’s family, said he was en route to the US. “The plane is in flight,” Metrópoles reported, without making clear where it had departed from.Bolsonaro allies told Metrópoles that he would land in Florida on Tuesday afternoon and planned to request political asylum. “The Donald Trump administration has been informed,” the website added.Lula condemned Bolsonaro’s apparent decision to flee. “This is what the family Bolsonaro are like. Brazil is their second homeland. Their first homeland is licking the boots of the US, as he’s become accustomed to doing,” he said at an event celebrating his 81st birthday in Brasília.“I keep imagining what’s on the conscience of a citizen who just lost the elections and flees his country … He who owes nothing, fears nothing. A citizen who sneaks out of his country owes something. The act of leaving Brazil is shameful.”Allies also confirmed to the Folha de S Paulo newspaper that Bolsonaro was on his way to the US, and said the escape plan had been “organized and enabled by a lawyer close to the Bolsonaro clan”.“They say the flight should land in a few hours,” the newspaper added.The news network CNN Brasil reported that Bolsonaro had fled to the US with his wife and two daughters in the early hours of this morning.A US state department spokesperson said Bolsonaro and his family would be granted visas “to allow them entry into the United States”.Lawmakers from Lula’s Workers’ party asked the supreme court to order Bolsonaro’s arrest and requested that his name be put on Interpol’s Red Notice list.Bolsonaro had not been seen since Monday and missed a Tuesday-morning deadline to hand his passport to the federal police, fuelling rumours that he may have fled Brazil after losing on Sunday.A report in the Brazilian newspaper O Globo said that during a meeting with friends and lawyers on Monday, the defeated candidate had appeared “possessed and made it clear he was afraid of being arrested”.A supreme court justice cancelled Bolsonaro’s passport minutes after the result in a ruling related to a criminal case against the senator. He had until 11am to surrender the document to the federal police, but did not appear.Bolsonaro has had Italian citizenship since 2023 and reportedly possesses a passport from the European country.The Argentinian news website Infobae reported that on Monday night he reportedly fled to Argentina, where he was expected to board a private jet in Puerto Iguazú bound for the US, but the plane did not take off.Bolsonaro, who has yet to concede defeat to Lula, posted a video on Monday in which, commenting on the cancellation of his passport, he said: “I never thought about leaving the country.”One of the senator’s brothers, the former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro, who is in self-imposed exile in the US, had said in an interview last Friday that his brother should leave Brazil if he lost.The Brazilian newspaper Folha de S Paulo reported that allies in the Bolsonaro family’s inner circle had been told that he had indeed left for Argentina and intended to travel from there to the US.As there is no record of him passing through any regular Brazilian immigration checkpoint, the federal police are trying to establish from Argentinian authorities whether there is any record of him entering the country.The Argentinian channel Todo Noticias reported that the senator had reportedly crossed the border into Argentina on foot and abandoned plans to board the plane once news of his movements leaked.Bolsonaro was told to surrender his passport over a criminal case in which the federal police are investigating him for possible involvement in a money-laundering scheme worth about £680m ($905m) involving betting companies.skip past newsletter promotionafter newsletter promotionThe senator’s possible flight makes the future of the far right after the presidential election even more uncertain. The family patriarch, Jair Bolsonaro, is under house arrest for attempting a coup, and one of his sons is in the US and the whereabouts of another unclear.Eduardo Bolsonaro has an outstanding arrest warrant against him in Brazil, after being sentenced to four years in prison for trying to interfere in his father’s trial by lobbying Donald Trump to impose sanctions on the justices hearing the case.Political scientist Magna Inácio, a professor at the Federal University of Minas Gerais, believes a power vacuum may now emerge within the right.“The resistance of Brazilian voters to handing victory to this more extremist camp sends a signal that the right leadership is now up for grabs,” she said.Since Jair Bolsonaro, then a career congressman with few laws to his name, surprisingly won the presidency in 2018, there has effectively been no right wing in Brazil, only the far-right Bolsonarismo movement.Camila Rocha, a political scientist who studies Brazil’s new right, believes the fact that three Bolsonaros are now potentially out of the picture could trigger a “shift in power” away from blood ties.“I think there is a tendency for power to move away from the sons,” said Rocha, noting that before the election, polls showed Jair Bolsonaro supporters preferred other potential candidates over his eldest son, including Jair Bolsonaro’s wife, Michelle Bolsonaro, who was recently elected senator, and the São Paulo governor, Tarcísio de Freitas.Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly did not want to run because he thought a presidential campaign would turn his life into “hell”, and believed his re-election to the senate was assured. But with Eduardo, his father’s “plan A”, now living in the US, the senator was chosen to run.Most observers agree that Flávio lacks his father’s charisma. He had a 24-year political career in which he passed very few laws as a state legislator and senator, and the only previous time he ran for executive office was for mayor of Rio de Janeiro in 2016, when he fainted during a televised debate and finished fourth.Speaking in Brasília, Bolsonaro’s campaign chief, senator Rogério Marinho, said he was surprised by reports of his candidate’s departure. “Because yesterday we talked about the need for Flávio, with the 60 million votes he received, to take on this role as leader of the opposition … since we were given a mandate by a significant part of the population,” he said.Asked whether he believed Bolsonaro could lead the opposition from abroad, he said: “María Corina Machado did it” with her country, Venezuela.Even in a family frequently embroiled in legal trouble he stood out, facing longstanding criminal allegations, including suspicions that he embezzled part of his staff’s salaries, as well as more recent accusations.Even so, 48.21% of Brazilians voted for Flávio Bolsonaro on Sunday, which many analysts see as both an anti-Lula vote and a vote for whomever Jair Bolsonaro had chosen.Inácio believes the struggle over the Bolsonaro legacy will also play out among family members who remain in Brazil, including Michelle and Bolsonaro’s other political sons, the senator-elect Carlos Bolsonaro and congressman-elect Jair Renan Bolsonaro, who publicly do not get along with their stepmother.“Michelle clearly has a political project of her own, but she is likely to face strong resistance from the two stepsons who are in congress. It is only a matter of time before tensions between them grow,” said the political scientist.

Brazil's defeated candidate Flavio Bolsonaro flees to US despite cancelled passports

Brazil's former presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro fled to the US, sources said Tuesday, despite his passports being cancelled after he failed to comply with a Supreme Court order to hand them over as part of a money laundering probe. Bolsonaro's whereabouts had been a source of speculation since his election defeat on Sunday to leftist incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. 

Issued on: 27/10/2026 - 17:33
Modified: 27/10/2026 - 22:49

  3 min
Reading time
Share
By:
FRANCE 24
Opposition presidential candidate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro speaks after the presidential runoff in Brasilia, Brazil, on October 25, 2026. © Eraldo Peres, AP

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election and refusing to comply with ​a Supreme Court order to hand over his passports, sources said Tuesday.

According to Brazilian daily Folha de São Paulo which cited sources close to the family, “the Trump administration is aware of Flavio Bolsonaro's departure for the United States and will grant asylum to the Liberal Party senator.” According to these sources, the ultra-conservative senator “is expected to arrive in Miami or Dallas in the coming hours. He is said to have travelled with his wife, Fernanda, and their two daughters.”

According to São Paulo's other major daily newspaper, O Estado, which also spoke with people close to the Bolsonaro clan, the extended family of the defeated presidential candidate did not learn of his departure until Tuesday and described his decision as “untimely”.

The Brasilia-based major daily Correio Brasiliense reported that Flavio Bolsonaro has arrived in the United States. “According to sources within the Federal Police interviewed by the Correio, this operation was reportedly coordinated by Trump administration Secretary of State Marco Rubio,” the newspaper wrote.

A few hours later, the US State Department later said it would issue visas for the Bolsonaro family. "The State Department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States," a senior State Department official said

US President Donald Trump's administration has previously ⁠alleged that Flavio's father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.

Flavio's departure for the United States threatens to deepen a rift between the two most ‌populous nations in the Americas.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has accused Washington of colluding ⁠with the Bolsonaros to put them back in power, and Reuters reported ahead of Sunday's election on a US State Department campaign to restore them to office.

Lula reacted to Tuesday's news by calling it "shameful" for Flavio Bolsonoro to have left Brazil. He said that his rival in Sunday's presidential election should have stayed and proven his innocence.

Watch moreComeback kid: How did Brazil's veteran leader Lula upset Bolsonaro?

Bolsonaro was favoured to win Sunday's presidential election but ​ended up losing in a shock result to leftist Lula. On Monday, he was given ‌24 hours to hand in his passports as part of a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing, but that deadline lapsed, two other sources said, leading to his documents being cancelled.

Read moreFlavio Bolsonaro vows to lead opposition after Brazil court imposes travel ban

Former president Jair Bolsonaro also went to the United States after refusing to concede to Lula in 2022, when former US president Joe ​Biden was in office. He eventually returned to Brazil but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.

His son has yet to officially concede defeat – saying on Sunday he ​would seek the annulment of the result over alleged voter irregularities – but his Liberal Party said on Monday it acknowledged ​Lula's victory.

It remains unclear how Bolsonaro was able to leave the country while ​he was facing a 24-hour Supreme Court deadline to hand over his passports. A senior Brazilian Federal Police official said Bolsonaro had not exited the country via any regular ​migration point.

Right-wing influencer Paulo Figueiredo, who serves as a sort of unofficial spokesperson for the Bolsonaro family, declined to answer questions about Bolsonaro's whereabouts.

"After months of intense work that has been unfairly thwarted, I am not in the mood to speak to the press," he said in a message. "If I have any comments to make on any matter, I will get in ⁠touch."

Eduardo Bolsonaro, Bolsonaro's younger brother who lives in the United States, said ahead of the vote that an election loss would require a move.

"If ⁠my brother does not ​win, I'm in favour that he would leave the country," he told podcaster Steven Crowder this month.

(FRANCE 24 with Reuters)

sources.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro reportedly leaves Brazil for US after election defeat
sources.text:
Published on 27 October 2026 - 17:03 GMT+1•Updated
22:24
Flávio Bolsonaro has left Brazil for the United States following his defeat in Sunday's presidential election, according to multiple media reports.
Bolsonaro's departure was confirmed to CNN and Reuters by US officials and to the Brazilian newspaper "Folha de São Paulo" by allies of the Bolsonaro family. The US State Department has reportedly said it would issue visas to him and his family.
The former presidential candidate is expected to arrive in the United States in the coming hours. According to Brazilian news outlet Metrópoles, his destination is Miami. He is reportedly travelling with his wife and two daughters.
Bolsonaro's passports were cancelled on Tuesday after Supreme Federal Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had ordered Bolsonaro to hand over his passports to Brazilian Federal Police (PF) in the wake of his election defeat to leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva over the weekend.
Bolsonaro agreed with his legal team that he would comply with the order and that he would deliver the documents to authorities on Tuesday morning, but he had failed to do so by Tuesday afternoon.
A police source told the AFP news agency that Bolsonaro's passports had now been "cancelled" and confirmed that there was "no formal record" of him leaving the country.
It comes after Argentine outlet Infobae reported that the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro had arrived in the Argentine town of Puerto Iguazú at 2 am on Tuesday, using his national identity card. He was reportedly preparing to continue on to the United States on a private flight.
According to Infobae, the aircraft was a Gulfstream G400, registration LV-JQW, owned by the company Baires Fly SA, which requested customs clearance for four passengers and three crew members.
The plane left Buenos Aires for Puerto Iguazú on Monday at 10:20 pm.
Since early Tuesday morning, Bolsonaro's allies have been trying to contact him, without success, according to Letícia Casado, a columnist for the UOL news website.
Euronews has contacted the PF for comment.
Rogério Marinho, Bolsonaro's general campaign coordinator, has denied that Bolsonaro has left Brazil.
Argentina's government has also rejected the claims.
On Friday, two days before the second round of the presidential election, Bolsonaro's brother Eduardo argued that he should leave Brazil if he were defeated. Eduardo has been living in the US since 2025, after being sentenced to prison by Brazil's Supreme Federal Court for coercion in the case involving his father Jair's attempts to overturn the results of the 2022 election.
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the Brazilian election looked "rigged," without providing evidence.
Speaking to the media, Trump said the vote "looked terrible" and "like another rigged election."
"I didn't take sides," Trump told reporters when asked for his thoughts. "Elections have to be indisputable, and it looked very bad to me."
Bolsonaro initially refused to recognise Lula's victory, saying it was "impossible" to acknowledge the result and that the election should have been annulled. He later said he would "organise the opposition."
In a video post shared on social media on Monday, he added that he had been banned from leaving Brazil and had been "served a notice to surrender my passports."

Published: 1:41am, 28 Oct 2026Updated: 6:01am, 28 Oct 2026

Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country ⁠for the US after losing Sunday’s ⁠presidential election, three sources said on Tuesday afternoon, with the ⁠US State Department due to grant him and his family entry visas.

Bolsonaro, who has yet to concede to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, left Brazil after refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.

The ruling relates to a money-laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing.

The location of Flavio, his wife and two daughters was not immediately clear. One source close to the ‌family said Flavio had landed in Florida, but declined to say where.

“The State Department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States,” a senior State Department official said.

Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro speaks in Brasilia on Sunday after losing the run-off election. Photo: Reuters

Bolsonaro’s departure threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas.

Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to put them back in power, and Reuters reported ahead of Sunday’s election on a US State Department campaign to restore them to office.

Trump has previously alleged Flavio’s father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in ⁠Brazil.

The elder Bolsonaro also went to the US after refusing to concede to Lula in 2022, when former US president Joe Biden was in office. ‌He eventually returned but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.

Trump made no mention of Flavio Bolsonaro’s departure in comments to the press on Monday, but said the Brazilian vote “looked like another ‌rigged election”.

Lula, speaking in Brasilia, said he had just heard that Flavio had left the country, and called it shameful, saying he should ⁠have stayed in Brazil and proved ⁠his innocence.

Bolsonaro was favoured to win Sunday’s presidential election but ended up losing in a shock result to Lula.

On Monday, he was given 24 hours to surrender his ‌passports, but they were cancelled after the deadline lapsed, two sources said.

In a court ruling seen by Reuters, the Supreme Court cited the risk of Bolsonaro fleeing Brazil and his “significant financial resources” in ordering his passports seized.

02:35
Lula just made history in Brazil, but the biggest winner might be China

Bolsonaro, ‌who ‌loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, said on Monday he had no plans to flee.

“I have never thought about leaving the ‌country,” he said. “I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me.”

His departure appeared to have caught ⁠his campaign manager off guard.

“We are surprised by the news because, just yesterday, we discussed the need for Flavio – given the 60 million votes he received – to take ⁠on this role as leader of the opposition,” Senator Rogerio Marinho told reporters.

Although Bolsonaro has yet to officially concede defeat – saying on Sunday he would seek the annulment of the result over alleged voter irregularities – his Liberal Party said on Monday that it acknowledged Lula’s victory.

It remains unclear how Bolsonaro was ‌able to leave the country while he was facing a 24-hour Supreme Court deadline to hand over his passports.

A senior Brazilian ⁠Federal Police official said Bolsonaro had not exited the country via any regular migration point.

Eduardo Bolsonaro, Bolsonaro’s younger brother who lives in the ‌US, had said before ‌the vote that an election loss would require a move.

“If my brother does not win, I’m in favour that he would leave the country,” he told podcaster Steven Crowder this month.

sources.headline: U.S. issuing visas to Brazil's Flávio Bolsonaro and family, official says
sources.text:
Updated on: October 27, 2026 / 8:28 PM EDT
/ CBS/AP
Add CBS News on Google
Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and his family will receive U.S. visas after Bolsonaro lost Brazil's presidential election over the weekend, a senior State Department official told CBS News on Tuesday. Bolsonaro, an ally of President Trump, and his family will be allowed entry into the U.S., the official said. Bolsonaro departed Brazil for the U.S. following his loss to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday's election, according to multiple Brazilian media reports.A spokesperson for Bolsonaro did not respond to a request for comment. His campaign manager Rogério Marinho also refused to comment. Silva said Tuesday it was "shameful" that Bolsonaro had fled Brazil."A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide," Silva said, per Agence France-Presse. "The act of leaving Brazil is shameful."Bolsonaro's brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro, who lives in Texas, had publicly encouraged him to leave Brazil if he lost the election.
Bolsonaro has touted his relationship with Mr. Trump and visited the White House in May. The family connections go deeper: Brother Eduardo Bolsonaro was convicted in absentia in June of illegally lobbying the Trump administration and sentenced to four years in prison. A warrant was recently issued for his arrest.Mr. Trump did not offer a full-throated endorsement of Bolsonaro in the runoff against Lula, as he has with some other right-of-center candidates in Latin America. But he suggested on Monday, without providing evidence, that Brazil's election was "rigged."
Flávio Bolsonaro, a Brazilian presidential candidate, speaks during a press conference at the Liberal Party camp following the runoff election in Brasilia, Brazil, on Oct. 25, 2026.
Arthur Menescal / Bloomberg via Getty Images
Bolsonaro's decision to leave Brazil came as a deadline for him to surrender his regular and diplomatic passports expired at noon Tuesday. It remained unclear whether he had complied."This is what the Bolsonaro family is like: Brazil is their second nation, the U.S. is the first," Lula said Tuesday, according to Reuters.
Bolsonaro was served with the order to surrender his passports Monday, a day after his stunning loss. Bolsonaro said he received it outside the home where his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for attempting a coup following his 2022 election loss to Lula. After his 2022 defeat, Jair Bolsonaro fled Brazil for Florida. He returned three months later.The sealed Supreme Court order, viewed by The Associated Press, was issued Sunday. Bolsonaro has refused to concede defeat and has made unsubstantiated allegations of election fraud.Lula, who turned 81 on Tuesday, received more than 64 million votes, compared with fewer than 60 million for Bolsonaro, a margin of nearly 4%.

Jair Bolsonaro later returned to Brazil and was sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.

sources.headline: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
sources.text: Figure caption, ByIone WellsReporting fromBrasília and Hafsa KhalilBrazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office in a dramatic comeback over his right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.Left-wing leader Lula took 51.79% of votes, becoming the first president since Brazil's return to civilian rule in 1985 to be elected after losing the first round of voting.Lula told jubilant crowds his victory was a "loss for negativity, lies", adding "long live democracy".Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has so far refused to recognise the result and called for it to be annulled. World leaders have congratulated Lula on his re-election.Bolsonaro's rejection comes as no surprise to observers. His father did the same. But a challenge appears unlikely to succeed.Firstly, it seems to centre on the unprecedented decision by the Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting nationwide by two hours. Some Bolsonaro fans are pointing out that Zanin was once Lula's lawyer and alleging bias.But both teams had requested an extension to voting times - Lula's had argued that voters in São Paulo and Bahia could not get to the polling stations because of a lack of buses, while Bolsonaro's campaign cited heavy rain in some areas in the south of the country and in São Paulo as their reason.Both knew every vote would count and did not want their side to miss out.The president of the Supreme Electoral Court Kássio Nunes Marques – appointed by Jair Bolsonaro – confirmed Lula's victory and said that the voter extension did not change the outcome of the race.The sheer gap between the two candidates' tallies - 4.4 million votes - makes the result more difficult to challenge.Image source, ReutersImage caption, Lula is making history as the first Brazilian to be elected four timesThe result came as a surprise after Flávio Bolsonaro won the first round on 4 October with 47% of votes ahead of Lula's 45%.But Lula's camp gained momentum ahead of election day, focusing on boosting voter turnout after 33 million people did not vote in round one. Sunday saw the largest drop in abstention between the two rounds of a presidential election since 1989.Bolsonaro had been poised to give a victory speech and said the result should be annulled, calling it "inexplicable".As his disconsolate supporters left the house in Brasília where their candidate had been watching the result, Lula took to the streets in São Paulo to celebrate."This, my fourth term, will be the best of any president in the history of this country," the former metal worker told supporters. "It will be the one in which I listen most to the Brazilian people."After pulling off this victory, Lula faces big hurdles: a divided country, an opponent that won't recognise the result, and a hostile Congress packed full of Bolsonaro allies.Markets reacted negatively to the unexpected outcome. The Sao Paolo stock exchange opened 15% down, sparking a brief suspension before recovering slightly. Interest rate futures rose as investors scrutinised Lula's fiscal plans.Reacting to the result, US President Donald Trump suggested the election had been stolen."I didn't take sides, but it looked like another rigged election," he told reporters on Monday, without providing evidence or more details. "It looked very bad to me."Other world leaders from across the political spectrum have congratulated Lula. Mexico's left-wing President Claudia Sheinbaum said in a post on X: "The people of Brazil won."Peru's right-wing President Keiko Fujimori praised Brazil's "democratic day". Similar messages were shared by the presidents of Chile and Ecuador.Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted that their two countries had already "flourished under our partnership".European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said "democracy and multilateralism" had won. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez - also a left-wing leader - called it a "great victory".French President Emmanuel Macron said the two nations should work "in service of a more just world".South African President Cyril Ramaphosa called Lula's victory one for the "global south and progressive forces throughout the world". Image source, Bloomberg via Getty ImagesImage caption, Flávio Bolsonaro has refused to accept the result, calling for it to be annulledIn a video posted on Instagram later on Monday, Flávio Bolsonaro said police had told him to hand over his passports and had been banned from leaving the country. Trump has previously shown support for Bolsonaro's father Jair, who is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence after being convicted of a coup attempt after losing the 2022 elections to Lula. Flávio Bolsonaro met Trump at the White House earlier this year to bid for his support.Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, has already been president for three non-consecutive terms, serving two terms between January 2003 to December 2010, and again from January 2023.His win makes him the first in Brazilian history to secure a fourth term, which will last until 2030.But this has been a bitterly fought campaign and the new term - set to start on 5 January - comes amid significant constraints at home and abroad, including animosity from the US president.Referring to what Trump has called the "Donroe Doctrine" - which seeks to establish US dominance in the Western Hemisphere - Lula used his victory speech to insist that Brazil "will not accept being anyone's backyard".Lula has also bucked a wider trend in Latin America, where voters in countries such as Argentina, Chile and Colombia have put right-wing candidates and parties in power.

sources.headline: Brazil's left-wing President Lula elected for fourth term
sources.text:
Supporters of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva cheer as the results of Brazil's presidential runoff election are announced in São Paulo on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026.
Natacha Pisarenko/AP
hide caption
Natacha Pisarenko/AP
BRASILIA, Brazil — In a stunning political comeback, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has been elected president of Brazil, according to official results from Sunday's runoff election, with more than 96% of the votes counted. Lula secured more than 51% of the vote, defeating Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, who received more than 48%. The result marks a historic moment in Brazil's democratic era. Since democracy was restored in 1989, no candidate who failed to win the first round of voting has gone on to win the presidency in the second round. The victory also adds another chapter to Lula's long political career, securing him a fourth, nonconsecutive presidential term. Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, will be among the oldest sitting leaders in the Americas, alongside President Trump and Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega, both 80.
In a speech to ecstatic supporters in São Paulo, Lula said the election was a "defeat of denialism. A defeat of lies." "I want to thank the Brazilian people for this generosity they have shown me for so long, to thank the youth who took to the streets to defend democracy, and the elders who went to vote," Lula told the crowd.
President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva addresses supporters after winning a fourth term in the presidential runoff in , Brazil, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026.
Andre Penner/AP
hide caption
Andre Penner/AP
Lula's victory bucks a broader rightward shift across Latin America in recent years. In a pointed message to Trump, Lula declared that Brazil would not accept being "anyone's backyard." A bitterly divided election Election day unfolded chaotically. Around midday, Lula's campaign requested an extension of voting hours, arguing that some local governments had reduced bus services, making it harder for voters to reach polling stations. Bolsonaro also sought an extension, citing heavy rain in some states. Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin extended voting by two hours, to 7 p.m., but some polling stations had already deactivated their electronic voting machines and could not resume voting. Speaking briefly to journalists outside his home in Brasilia, Bolsonaro called the result "inexplicable" and said he would seek to annul the vote. "I will not give up on my Brazil, and I hope you won't give up either," he said.
Bolsonaro, 45, had campaigned on closer ties with President Trump and pledged to pardon his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for plotting a coup to overturn his 2022 election defeat to Lula.
Opposition presidential candidate Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro speaks after the presidential runoff in , Brazil, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026.
Eraldo Peres/AP
hide caption
Eraldo Peres/AP
Brazilians showed little enthusiasm for street campaigning in the early months. But Bolsonaro's first-round finish on Oct. 4 energized the contest, and in recent days supporters of both candidates have filled rallies and flooded social media in an effort to sway voters. In the end, Lula's message of continuity and a focus on social spending prevailed. "I think people woke up about the risk of a Bolsonaro government after the first round, and the mobilization made a difference," said Alessandra Miguel, a 35-year-old spa worker who voted for Lula in Rocinha, a favela in Rio de Janeiro. From union leader to president Lula rose to national prominence as the leader of a metalworkers' union that organized strikes that helped bring down Brazil's dictatorship in the 1980s. Unions and progressive Catholic activists joined forces at the time to form the Workers' Party, which Lula has now represented in seven presidential elections. During Lula's first two terms in office, from 2003 to 2010, Brazil's economy boomed, and millions of Brazilians rose out of poverty. But many voters turned their backs on the party when Lula and other leaders became embroiled in corruption scandals in the 2010s. Lula himself was jailed, though his convictions were later overturned on procedural grounds. On foreign policy, Lula has worked to boost the political influence of countries in the Global South as a founding member of the BRICS group, a grouping of major emerging economies that includes Brazil, China, Russia, India and South Africa. He has argued that Brazil should maintain friendly relations with all major world powers, though his ties with China and Russia have sometimes led him to clash with Washington.
Supporters of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva celebrate after he wins a fourth term in the presidential runoff in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026.
Silvia Izquierdo/AP
hide caption
Silvia Izquierdo/AP
Lula's approval rating rose after he stood up to Trump, but his disapproval rating remained higher than his approval rating at the start of the election season. Brazil's economic growth has been slower than during Lula's first two terms, and many Brazilians felt he had not done enough to address crime and public security.
During the campaign, Lula sought to address those concerns by proposing a ban on sports betting, announcing a debt renegotiation program and backing tougher penalties for minors who commit crimes. He will govern a sharply divided country. Brazilian political scientist Jairo Nicolau, who studies presidential elections, said one of the most striking features of this year's contest was the rigidity of Brazilians' political allegiances. Unlike in past years, Nicolau said, "people's identity of belonging to a tribe became more important than how they view different policy options."

sources.text: Ana Ionova, Adam B. Ellick and Jack NicasLula won Brazil’s election after a huge social media push, with a WhatsApp network growing from a few thousand to 10 million supporters.His victory beat Flavio Bolsonaro and blocked the Bolsonaro family’s return, after voters feared threats to democracy and a possible rewrite of Brazil’s constitution.The vote was chaotic and contested, with delays, legal threats and claims of bias, but officials said Brazil’s electronic voting system remained secure.AI generatedRio de Janeiro – It started with a WhatsApp channel with a few thousand followers.
